name: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
notes: The record's title and claim.quote are the verbatim title of Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015), which contains the word 'Discovery'.

published.quote: This paper has been published in Phys. Rev Lett. 115 121802 (2015)

significance.locator: arXiv:1507.01417 (PDF), Conclusions, p. 6; the same figure is given in the Results section, pp. 5-6. The abstract says only 'larger than 5 σ'.
significance.note: The abstract states only a significance larger than 5 σ. The figure 5.1 σ is given in the body of the paper: in the Results section both test statistics (a combination of the per-channel p-values, one-sided, and a profile likelihood ratio) give 5.1 standard deviations, and the Conclusions state it as the significance of the discovery.
significance.quote: Given the low background level and the observed number of ντ candidate events, we report the discovery of a ντ appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with a significance of 5.1 σ.

summary.plain: OPERA reports the discovery of tau-neutrino appearance in the muon-neutrino beam sent from CERN to the Gran Sasso laboratory: five tau-neutrino candidate events against an expected background of about 0.25 events, at a significance the paper puts at 5.1σ (its abstract says only that it is larger than 5σ).
summary.technical: OPERA νμ→ντ appearance analysis of the CNGS data taken from 2008 to 2012: a fifth ντ candidate event found in an enlarged data sample; five candidates observed against a total background expectation of 0.25 ± 0.05 events (expected signal 2.64 ± 0.53 events for Δm²23 = 2.44×10⁻³ eV² and sin²2θ23 = 1), corresponding to the discovery of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode with a significance of 5.1σ (stated in the Results and Conclusions; the abstract says larger than 5σ).

title: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
why_it_matters: The paper says the observation of νμ→ντ appearance with four candidate events had been reported previously (its introduction calls the earlier 4.2σ claim the first observation of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode); the fifth candidate, together with a further reduction of the expected background, raises the significance to 5.1σ, which the paper reports as the discovery of νμ→ντ appearance.
